keys.statement: Across the Pfizer, GSK and Sanofi guides, water, n-propyl and isopropyl acetate and 1- and 2-butanol are rated green, while chlorinated solvents, NMP, DMF, DMAc, benzene, hexane, 1,4-dioxane and diethyl ether are undesirable.

decisions.mechanism: Health, safety and environmental ratings differ widely.
decisions.operation: Prefer the green list; justify any undesirable solvent.
limits: NMP and DMF, rated undesirable here, are the extractive solvents studied in Li 2017; a trade-off to report, not a contradiction of results.

verification_required: An AI review session checks the statement against byrne-2016-solvent-selection-guides, Unified guides, pp. 8-9 (Figs. 6-7).

keys.statement: Where an ether solvent is needed, 2-methyltetrahydrofuran and tert-butyl methyl ether are preferred to tetrahydrofuran and diethyl ether.

decisions.obstacle: Ether solvents with poor hazard profiles.
decisions.mechanism: Safer ethers exist with similar function.

verification_required: An AI review session checks the statement against byrne-2016-solvent-selection-guides, Unified guides, p. 9.

keys.statement: Whether to recover a waste solvent by distillation or incinerate it depends on the energy embodied in making it: recovering tetrahydrofuran saves energy, while diethyl ether is better incinerated.

decisions.mechanism: Production energy differs strongly between solvents.
decisions.operation: Compare recovery energy with production energy.
